If I witness a child being born 5 light years away and then travel to him at the speed of light, how old would the child be from his perspective when I arrive? Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.assistant

Let's break down the problem step by step.

    From your perspective, you witness the birth of the child 5 light years away. This means that, from your perspective, the child is born at a distance of 5 light years.

    Now, you travel to the child at the speed of light. Since you're traveling at the speed of light, time dilation occurs, and time appears to pass more slowly for you relative to outside observers.

    From your perspective, as you approach the child, time appears to pass normally. You see the child grow up, and you arrive at the child's location.

    However, from the child's perspective, time dilation occurs. Since you're traveling at the speed of light, time appears to pass normally for you, but it appears to pass more slowly for the child.

    The child will experience time passing normally, while you experience time passing normally as well. This means that, from the child's perspective, you will arrive at the same age as when you left.

    In other words, the child will not experience any age difference between when you left and when you arrive. You will arrive at the same age as when you left.

    So, from the child's perspective, you will arrive at the same age as when you left, which is 0 years old.

    Note that this is a consequence of special relativity, and it's a mind-bending effect that can be difficult to wrap your head around.
